req.title: POST-only actions reject GET
req.statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 405 when GET is used on /<id>/delete.

doc.reasoning: The requirement states that GET requests to /<id>/delete must return HTTP 405. The delete route in blog.py is registered with methods=('POST',) only, so Flask will automatically return 405 for GET. Tests cover: (1) positive case — POST to delete works for authenticated author (verifying the route accepts POST), (2) negative case — GET to /<id>/delete returns exactly 405 for an unauthenticated client, (3) boundary case — GET to /<id>/delete returns exactly 405 even when the user IS authenticated (ruling out auth redirect masking the 405), (4) additional negative — GET with a valid post id by the post's author still returns 405, not 200 or 302. Mutation resilience: all assertions use exact status code 405 (catches constant mutations like 404->405, 405->403), and we verify POST succeeds with 302 (catches method-check bypass mutations).

tests.name: test_get_delete_unauthenticated_returns_405
preconditions: App is running in TESTING mode with a fresh database
actions: Send GET request to /1/delete without logging in
expected: HTTP 405 Method Not Allowed is returned
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_get_delete_unauthenticated_returns_405():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.get('/1/delete')
    assert r.status_code == 405

test_get_delete_unauthenticated_returns_405()

import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_get_delete_authenticated_author_returns_405():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    login_r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Rahul', 'password': 'stone'})
    assert login_r.status_code == 302
    r = client.get('/2/delete')
    assert r.status_code == 405

test_get_delete_authenticated_author_returns_405()

expected: Status code is exactly 302, confirming POST is accepted

from flaskr import create_app

def test_post_delete_authenticated_author_succeeds_not_405():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    login_r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Rahul', 'password': 'stone'})
    assert login_r.status_code == 302
    r = client.post('/2/delete')
    assert r.status_code == 302
    assert r.status_code != 405

tests.name: test_get_delete_nonexistent_id_returns_405_not_404
preconditions: App is running in TESTING mode with a fresh database
actions: Send GET request to /9999/delete (non-existent post id)
expected: HTTP 405 is returned because method check precedes existence check
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_get_delete_nonexistent_id_returns_405_not_404():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.get('/9999/delete')
    assert r.status_code == 405
    assert r.status_code != 404
    assert r.status_code != 302
    assert r.status_code != 200
